query: What travel policy risks appear in expense descriptions?

per_column.name: asset_category
per_column.rationale: Categorises the asset/item type from ci and short_description; well-grounded in the samples. Only partly aligned with the travel-policy-risk query, but the travel_item bucket does isolate the relevant subset, giving some analytical leverage.

per_column.name: transport_expense_misclassified
per_column.rationale: Directly targets a travel policy risk (transport expenses miscoded), so highly useful. However determining misclassification generally requires comparing description against category; the samples shown are all trivially False and the basis for the 14 True flags is not demonstrated, so groundedness is moderate with inference risk.

per_column.name: asset_description_quality
per_column.rationale: A quality/specificity axis of the description is a reasonable reading of the text (specific model vs travel descriptor vs vague). Relevant to policy risk since vague descriptions are a compliance flag. Grounded in the samples.

per_column.name: entry_method
per_column.rationale: Manual vs automated is inferable from short_description phrasing ('Automated'/'Automatically'), so reasonably grounded. But entry method has weak bearing on travel policy risk, limiting analytical value for this query.

per_column.name: missing_source_id_flag
per_column.rationale: A near-mechanical restatement of whether source_id is empty in an existing column; well-grounded but low leverage and largely redundant with the original source_id field, and only tangentially about travel policy.

per_column.name: processing_lag_flag
per_column.rationale: Derived from date fields but the threshold/basis for 'lag' is opaque and one sample without a processed_date is False rather than unknown. Weakly connected to travel policy risk specifically.

per_column.name: repeat_user_flag
per_column.rationale: Repeat submitters can be a genuine axis for expense/travel abuse analysis, giving some leverage. Derivable from the user column across rows, though not verifiable in the single-row samples.

judge.rationale: Several columns (transport_expense_misclassified, asset_description_quality, asset_category, repeat_user_flag) give genuine axes for spotting travel policy risks in expense descriptions, while others (missing_source_id_flag, processing_lag_flag, entry_method) are more generic infrastructure/quality flags with weak ties to the query. Most values are sound readings of the source text; the main groundedness concern is transport_expense_misclassified, whose True cases and inference basis are not evidenced in the samples.
